message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to sell houses or declare bankruptcy for a $100 rent shortfall.

One house sells for $50, leaving a $7 shortfall. Two houses sell for $100, covering the debt and leaving $43 cash. I need to check if building rules require selling evenly.

Standard Monopoly rules require houses to be built and sold evenly across a color group. Selling two houses from one property would leave a difference of two, which is illegal. I must sell one house from two different properties instead.

Selling one house from St. Charles and one from States Avenue keeps the group evenly split at 2-2-3. Virginia Avenue retains its three houses to preserve the $500 rent spike. I am now recalling the standard rent values for pink properties.

Virginia Avenue's rent drops from $500 to $180 when it loses a house, so keeping three houses there is critical. St. Charles and States Avenue each pay $450 with three houses, falling to $150 each with two. Selling one house from each of those two properties yields exactly $100, covering the $57 shortfall while preserving Virginia's high rent.

I will sell one house from St. Charles Place and one from States Avenue. Selling more would break the even distribution or destroy Virginia's high rent. p2 is the main threat with dark blues and reds at full houses. The other players lack complete monopolies.
